title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lovell, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lovell, WY | Elk Basin Field
metaDescription: Lovell, WY mineral owner near the Elk Basin field in Big Horn County? Get a fair cash offer for your Bighorn Basin mineral or royalty interest.
heroLead: Lovell sits near Elk Basin field, one of the Bighorn Basin's early giant discoveries, straddling the Wyoming-Montana line at the basin's northern edge.
intro: Elk Basin has been producing since 1915, one of the structural traps that made this stretch of Big Horn County an early Wyoming oil center. A century of production has left plenty of paper trail behind, and plenty of small, split ownership interests along with it.

sections.heading: Elk Basin's long production history
paragraphs: Like the basin's other legacy anticline fields, Elk Basin has moved from primary production to secondary and even tertiary recovery methods over its lifetime, extending well life far past what the original 1910s discovery would have supported alone. Current output is mature and stripper-level, operated by independents working the legacy leases.

sections.heading: Cross-border complications
paragraphs: Because Elk Basin field crosses the Wyoming-Montana state line, some Lovell-area mineral owners hold interests governed partly by Wyoming law and partly by Montana law depending on exact tract location. Confirming which state's rules apply to your specific section matters for tax and legal purposes.

sections.heading: Preparing to sell
paragraphs: Bring your deed, division order, and recent check stubs if you have them. Big Horn County Clerk records in Basin can confirm Wyoming-side history; if your tract crosses into Montana, additional records may be needed from the appropriate Montana county.

sections.heading: Working across a state line courthouse
paragraphs: If your family's Elk Basin-area tract straddles into Montana, you may need records from a Montana county clerk in addition to Big Horn County. It's an extra step worth taking early, since a buyer's title review will need clarity on which state's law governs your specific portion of the interest.

faqs.question: Is Elk Basin field still producing after a century?
faqs.answer: Yes, at mature stripper levels, with secondary recovery methods having extended the field's productive life well beyond its original discovery era.

faqs.question: Does my interest fall on the Wyoming or Montana side?
faqs.answer: Check your legal description against the state line, or ask the Big Horn County Clerk in Basin to help confirm which state's records govern your specific tract.

faqs.question: How does a century of ownership transfers affect selling now?
faqs.answer: It mainly means more prior transactions to trace through title. A buyer will want your current deed and any division order to move efficiently through that history.

faqs.question: Which Montana county would hold records for the cross-border portion?
faqs.answer: It depends on your exact legal description; Carbon County, Montana is the likely reference point for the Elk Basin area, but confirm against your specific township and range.
